tasks.passage: On a summer afternoon, the center of a large city can be several degrees {warmer|colder|wetter} than the countryside around it. Scientists call this the urban heat island {effect|reason|story}. Dark roads and roofs {absorb|reflect|forget} sunlight during the day and release the heat slowly at night. Cities also have fewer trees, which {cool|warm|hide} the air when water evaporates from their leaves. In addition, cars and air conditioners {produce|remove|prevent} heat of their own.

missing_sentence.answer: This extra heat can be dangerous for older people and young children during heat waves.
wrong: Many families enjoy visiting the countryside on summer weekends.

tasks.rest: Some cities are now fighting back. Paris and Los Angeles have painted streets and roofs in light colors that send sunlight back into the sky. Other cities plant thousands of trees each year and turn empty lots into small parks. These changes cost money, but they can lower summer temperatures by one or two degrees. That may not sound like much, but on the hottest days it can mean fewer people in hospital.

highlight.answer: absorb sunlight during the day and release the heat slowly at night

highlight.question: How much can these changes lower summer temperatures?

tasks.passage: Daniel had played the violin for six years, but he had never played {alone|together|loudly} in front of an audience. When his teacher asked him to perform at the school concert, he {agreed|refused|forgot} before he had time to think. For the next three weeks, he {practiced|avoided|explained} the same piece every evening. On the night of the concert, his hands were {shaking|sleeping|singing} as he walked onto the stage. He looked at the crowd and could not {remember|return|receive} the first note.

tasks.scenario: You are a student in an introductory biology course. Last Thursday you were sick with the flu, so you missed the weekly lab session. In that lab, the class measured how fast plants grow under different colors of light. Your lab report is due next Monday, and you want to ask your professor how you can make up the work.

complete.sentence: You missed the lab session because you ___.
In the lab, the class measured how fast ___.
complete.answer: plants grow under different colors of light

you.answer: Hi, Professor Lee. Do you have a few minutes? I wanted to ask about last week's lab.
wrong: Hey, what's up? I need the lab stuff from last week, okay?
Hello, Professor Lee. I wanted to ask about the final exam next month.

conversation.partner: Of course. Come in. You weren't there on Thursday, were you?

you.answer: No, I wasn't. I had the flu, and I stayed home for two days.
wrong: Yes, I was there, but I left early to catch a bus.
No, I didn't come. I thought the lab was cancelled for the holiday.

conversation.partner: I'm sorry to hear that. Are you feeling better now?

you.answer: Yes, much better, thanks. I'm worried about the lab report, though.
wrong: Yes, they are feeling much better now, thank you.
No, but I'm not worried about the lab report at all.

conversation.partner: That's understandable. The report needs data from the experiment, so you can't write it without doing the lab.

you.answer: Is there another time when I could do the experiment?
wrong: Could I write the report without any data, then?
Can you tell me when the library opens tomorrow?

conversation.partner: Yes. The Tuesday lab group meets tomorrow at two. You can join them, and I'll tell the teaching assistant to expect you.

you.answer: That would be great. Should I still hand in the report on Monday?
wrong: That would be great. I'll join the Thursday group next week, then.
Thanks, but I'd rather not do the experiment at all.

conversation.partner: No, take an extra two days. Send it to me by Wednesday.

you.answer: Thank you so much. I'll see the teaching assistant tomorrow at two.
wrong: Thank you. I'll send the report by next Monday, as planned.
Okay. I'll see you at the Tuesday lab next week.

tasks.scenario: You and your classmate Jordan are preparing a group presentation about recycling for your environmental science class. The presentation is on Friday morning. Jordan agreed to make the slides, but Jordan has just started a part-time job and has had very little free time. You meet at the student center to decide what to do.

complete.sentence: Jordan has little free time because of ___.

conversation.partner: Hey, thanks for meeting me. I have some bad news about the slides.

you.answer: Oh no. What happened? Didn't you have time to finish them?
wrong: Great! I knew you would finish the slides early.
Hey. I can't meet today, sorry. Maybe next week?

conversation.partner: Not really. I've worked almost every evening since I started at the bookstore. I've only made four slides.

you.answer: That's okay. How many slides do we need in total?
wrong: That's okay. How many hours do you work at the café?
Four slides is too many for a short presentation.

conversation.partner: About twelve, I think. The professor said the talk should be ten minutes long.

you.answer: Then why don't I make the slides about plastic, and you finish the ones about paper?
wrong: Then let's ask the professor to cancel our presentation.
Then you should quit your job so that you can finish the slides.

conversation.partner: That would really help. But when can we practice together? I work tonight and tomorrow night.

you.answer: We could meet on Thursday before class and practice it twice.
wrong: We could meet on Saturday, after the presentation.
We don't need to practice, since you already know everything.

conversation.partner: Thursday works. I'll send you my four slides tonight so you can see the style.

you.answer: Perfect. I'll use the same colors and fonts so everything matches.
wrong: Perfect. I'll use different colors so people know who made each slide.
Please don't send them. I'd rather not see them.

conversation.partner: Great. I feel much better now. Thanks for being so understanding.

you.answer: No problem. Good luck at work tonight, and see you on Thursday.
wrong: No problem. See you on Friday afternoon, after the presentation.
You're welcome. Good luck with your exam tomorrow.
